# Language support at a glance

Generated from the same discovered providers, definitions, scope passages and test associations as the matrices. Expand a language's evidence for exact features and tests. This is bounded support, not a completeness score.

[Provider and transformer matrices](providers.md) · [Full capability details](provider-capabilities.md) · [Test runs and observation artifacts](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/actions/workflows/go.yml)

Available stages are discovered implementations. **Supported features and exclusions are owner-authored scope**, not conclusions inferred from rule names. Syntax support does not imply semantic analysis or generation support. **Test counts are associated declarations**, not passing results or coverage percentages. Delegate evidence does not qualify wrappers.

This committed view contains no execution results. Existing CI artifacts pair invocation reports with compact overviews; those retain source/build applicability and process failures. An absent observation does not mean a test never ran.

**[Scope: docs/syntax.md#c](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/syntax.md#c)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Includes, namespaces, records, type aliases, enums, type templates, fields,
method/destructor declarations and structured pointer/reference/array/function
declarators have syntax tooling, including dependent-name disambiguators.

**Exclusions / limits:** Non-type/template-template parameters, parameter packs, specialization,
constraints/requires expressions, computed array bounds, initializers,
constructors, operator declarations, macros and function bodies are outside
this slice. Qualified member-function-pointer types are rejected because native
FunctionType has no method CV/ref fields. The maintained native text gates
provide separately scoped compiler qualification.

**[Scope: docs/native-semantics.md#first-go-profile](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/native-semantics.md#first-go-profile)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** The supported subset remains the captured type-declaration fragment: one supplied
package across at most 16 files, defined types and aliases, generic parameters and
applications, named/predeclared types, slices, ordinary struct fields and tags,
embedded interface type terms, approximations and unions. Under an explicit
import environment, the captured files form several packages by their file paths,
and named and aliased imports of captured or explicitly supplied packages bind
qualified type references to the imported declarations.

**Exclusions / limits:** Imports outside an explicit import environment, dot and blank imports, the
standard library, methods, embedded struct fields, pointer/array/map/function
types and executable bodies remain unsupported. Syntax acceptance does not
promise semantic coverage.

**[Scope: docs/syntax.md#go](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/syntax.md#go)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Imports, defined types and aliases, generic parameters/applications, structs,
interfaces and method signatures, function types, pointers, slices, literal-length
arrays, maps, channels and constraint unions/approximations have structured syntax
tooling.

**Exclusions / limits:** Array lengths are literal integers in this initial vocabulary. Constant
expressions, constant/variable/function declarations, method implementations
and statements are outside this slice.

**[Scope: docs/analysis.md#horos-profile](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/analysis.md#horos-profile)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** The unified Horos profile exports general kinds as provider-owned terms and
facts. Semantic sort, declared contract, checked symbolic body and individual
memberships are separate relations. Type and kind definitions have distinct
provider-owned entity categories. No single fact is a principal inferred kind.
Membership facts retain their assumptions; missing facts assert nothing.
Program validity includes Horos's symbolic obligations on open declarations.
A syntactically valid `Forward<T> = DataPage<T>` can therefore be rejected before
specialization. Shared semantic carriers do not interpret these kind rules.

**Exclusions / limits:** The Horos syntax profile is `horos-declarations-4/ast-1`: optional semantic binding
annotations may be absent, while supplied annotations in the analyzed closure
must agree with analysis. The required entry/root selection is structural.
Analysis does not repair input or turn stale references into new references
silently. The explicit `resolve.Model` helper remains semantic and shares the
same authoritative path.

**[Scope: docs/horos-syntax.md#pipeline-and-limits](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/horos-syntax.md#pipeline-and-limits)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Syntax parsing constructs a lossless CST and AST view. Formatting constructs CST
from an AST view directly; the generic printer emits supplied leaves. The
provider composes independently registered Syntax/check/resolution/analysis
capabilities. [Files parsing and formatting](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/source.md) compose these stages over
several Program trees without creating a second language.

**Exclusions / limits:** Source is bounded to 4 MiB and 200,000 lexical tokens. Syntax/AST/CST and canonical
operations retain their separate limits. Failures return no usable partial
output. Function, Stream and Cell remain ordinary declarations with no parser or engine
special cases.

**[Scope: docs/horos.md#syntax-vocabulary](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/horos.md#syntax-vocabulary)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** The canonical module envelope remains revision, name, imports and declarations,
with revision 4. There is no schema-digest field. The AST retains Program roots,
module names/pins, imports, ordered parameters and literal Atom/Tuple fragments.
Module declarations now distinguish kind and type definitions.

**Exclusions / limits:** The old generic Declaration/Bound nodes and RoleBound are removed. Type/Data
names are ordinary references and never choose an AST variant. Primitive top
and sort syntax supplies the unconstrained proper default. Descriptor operands
still preserve the exact canonical value layout. Only Horos-designated type
positions contain type expressions; labels, scalar selectors, field wrappers and
`exact` payloads retain their literal roles.

**[Scope: docs/resolution.md#horos-composition](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/resolution.md#horos-composition)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Horos resolution accepts multiple separate Program trees and an explicit root entry, resolves its
reachable pinned module closure, verifies supplied annotations and exports exact
descriptor payloads and operand paths. Alongside `reference-resolution`, it
advertises the existing validity, declaration-index, occurrence-binding,
application, reference-dependency and type-fact evidence. General kind facts
separate sort, result sort, declared contract, result contract, checked symbolic
body and memberships with assumptions. Its owning resolver currently checks the
whole required program; a resolution-only request does not promise less work.

**Exclusions / limits:** Unknown imports/declarations can reject reference resolution. Other semantic
failures retain their own validity diagnostics and may leave reference resolution
incomplete. They are not automatically evidence of an unbound name. Missing
dependencies and resource exhaustion remain incomplete outcomes, not rejected
types. Export exhaustion preserves established reference resolution and program
validity without a model.

**[Scope: docs/native-semantics.md#first-rust-profile](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/native-semantics.md#first-rust-profile)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** The supported semantic fragment is one captured source file with inline modules,
type aliases, structs/tuple structs, enums with unit/tuple/record variants, fields,
ordinary type parameters and defaults, effective generic applications, paths,
primitives, tuples, numeric-length arrays, slices, raw pointers and explicit
`'static` references. Marker traits, supertraits, ordinary trait bounds/where
predicates and empty type-only trait impls are checked by the compiler. Sysroot
types use their compiler declaration identities: `Vec`, `Option`, `String`, `Box`
and similar types have no name-specific mapping in Bittype. Their internals stay
opaque; effective arguments include native defaults, such as an allocator argument.

**Exclusions / limits:** Imports and multi-file crates, dependency closures, methods/functions/callable
types, trait objects, associated types/projections/GATs, lifetime parameters,
non-static references, const generics and higher-ranked predicates are outside
this first semantic profile. Some have syntax tooling; that does not imply
semantic coverage. An unsupported source construct or exported compiler form
reports unsupported coverage without a partial graph. The standard compiler
prelude and sysroot are part of the explicit environment, not a library-name
switch in the kernel.

**[Scope: docs/syntax.md#rust](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/syntax.md#rust)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Type aliases, structs, enums, traits, generics and bounds; qualified associated-type
projections and equality bindings; generic associated-type declarations and
type-only trait impls with where clauses have structured syntax tooling.

**Exclusions / limits:** Unit structs have no distinct AST form and are rejected.
Const generics, higher-ranked binders, associated-type argument bounds
(`Iterator<Item: Clone>`), associated-type defaults, `impl Trait`, macros,
attributes, inherent/unsafe/negative/specializing impls, associated constants,
impl methods and executable bodies are outside this slice. Type-only trait
impls are the supported implementation form.

**[Scope: docs/native-semantics.md#first-typescript-profile](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/native-semantics.md#first-typescript-profile)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** The first profile covers aliases, interfaces and bases, generic parameters and
constraints, explicit applications, references, primitive/literal types, arrays,
tuples, object properties, unions, intersections and readonly arrays/tuples.
Script files share global scope; exported declarations give each file module
scope. Binders and declarations with the same spelling remain distinct symbols.
Named recursive types retain entity/fact links without cyclic term containment.

**Exclusions / limits:** Without the named-import configuration, imports and external package types are
unsupported. With it, named local/package imports and their supplied declarations
are admitted as described above. Qualified names, callable/method/index signatures, indexed access,
`keyof`, `unique`, `this`, generic defaults, interface declaration merging and
external types outside that explicit import environment or compiler-recognized array constructors remain
outside this first profile. Standard arrays and readonly arrays are supported;
mapped utility types such as `Readonly<T>` are not. Their synthesized modifiers
need a separate extension of native fact export. Authored conditional and mapped
types are also unsupported even though the syntax provider admits them.

**[Scope: docs/syntax.md#typescript](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/syntax.md#typescript)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Type-only imports, aliases and interfaces; generic parameters/applications;
objects, tuples, arrays, unions and intersections; function signatures, indexed
access and type operators; conditional/infer types and mapped types with key
remapping and modifier changes have structured syntax tooling.

**Exclusions / limits:** Template-literal types, value declarations, class bodies, decorators and
executable expressions remain outside this slice. See the
[text-tooling boundary](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/parsing-formatting.md#checks-and-admitted-syntax).

**[Scope: docs/typescript-type-imports.md#example-and-scope](https://github.com/Bitspark/bittype/blob/main/docs/typescript-type-imports.md#example-and-scope)** — profile: unspecified (authored profile absent).

**Supported features:** Move Person into `pages` in that placement and remove the empty model unit. The pages file now defines Person locally. Its import disappears and the Cell package import remains. Changing the model file's path changes the relative specifier. The returned Source records a local import relation at its actual import node for each owned module dependency. External packages retain their public specifiers and are supplied by the consuming build.

**Exclusions / limits:** This profile covers named type imports in nonempty, declaration-only TypeScript ESM modules. Output paths are Files-relative `.ts` paths, excluding `.d.ts` and URL delimiters `?`, `#` and `%`. Imports between output units use relative `.js` specifiers. Package declaration inputs support type aliases, interfaces and named type imports. Namespace imports, re-exports, runtime imports, ambient scripts and discovery of package files on disk are outside this profile.
